lead_headline: Weekend adds 8 restaurant leads—Vaultaire HiFi listening bar debuts, Paperboy brunch expands from Austin, Super Mega Bien closes after 8 years—as subscriptions stall (+4 since Friday) and foreclosures drop 19%

restaurant.blurb: 8 new leads since Friday bring active inventory to 75 (36 openings, 39 closures)—highest weekend haul in six weeks. Saturday's marquee: Vaultaire subterranean HiFi listening bar opens beneath La Forêt at 38 S Broadway (analog sound system, vintage spirits, French small plates); Paperboy Denver launches first-outside-Texas brunch outpost at 3453 W 32nd in Highlands. Weekend closures: Super Mega Bien RiNo Latin American staple shutters after 8 years citing financial pressures (4.6-star rating, March 14 close); Riot House Union Station nightclub marks December 2025 exit after sub-two-year run; Bar Amorina Cherry Creek cocktail bar flags 10-month Clayton Hotel tenure ended November. Openings cluster downtown corridors—Denver Café & Kava non-alcoholic kava bar preps 5501 E Colfax launch, Shuck Brothers oyster bar debuts permanent Avanti stall Sunday, Roll It Up Sushi truck-to-storefront conversion lands Edgewater Public Market. March's 75-lead tally surges 37% above February's 55-case month-end as scraping velocity accelerates through Q1 close.

foreclosure.blurb: 34 filings this week fall 19% from prior week's 42—March's softest period outside holiday windows—with top case at $686K Arapahoe property (24296 E Ohio) as zero $2M+ outliers mark first sub-million ceiling since mid-February.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend March's statewide drought to 30 consecutive days—now tracking 147% beyond any prior gap in 12,316-case archive. Tomorrow's April 1 quarterly deadline serves as critical inflection: sustained silence past Tuesday would confirm systemic database lag vs organic demand collapse across metro hospitality sector. Last comparable void: never—previous longest stretch capped at 12 days during 2024 winter holiday window.

reputation.blurb: 54 mentions this week climb 10% from prior period's 49—fourth consecutive weekly gain as Instagram claims 22% share (12 citations), matching Denver Post's 10 pickups. Top story cascade: Denver Summit NWSL inaugural sellout (63K attendance) drives 6 social pickups; San Antonio Express-News coworking feature cites BusinessDen data; Newmark/CBRE commercial hires thread through Polish aggregator prosteschody.pl. Week's 17 unique sources mark diversification shift—social platforms (Instagram, x.com, Facebook) now command 42% total vs legacy media's historical 60%+ dominance. Four-week rolling average settles at 47 mentions/week, projecting 2,444 annual citations if Q2 sustains March's acceleration.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +4 since Friday (5 new, 1 canceled) lifts MTD to +56 (+1.9/day), 90-day net to +125. Weekend stall pattern persists: Saturday-Sunday deliver zero net movement (1 new Saturday, 0 Sunday) following March 21-22 identical flatline—weekly cadence now concentrates 91% of acquisition Monday-Friday. Past 14 days split into distinct phases: March 16-20 surges +15 net (21 new, 6 canceled, 3.0/day pace) before March 23-29 moderates to +11 (23 new, 12 canceled, 1.6/day). Longer view: 90-day +125 tracks 39% ahead of YTD's +1.4/day baseline, but recent two-week churn acceleration (1.7 canceled/day vs 1.0 historical) suggests retention headwinds building into Q2. March needs +2 net across Monday-Tuesday to hit +58 monthly close, maintaining 32% premium over February's pace.
